blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Battlespace Sensing and Awareness' and offensive-cyber tooling assume live connectivity to targets/C2
blind_spots.operator_reality: Forward-deployed cyber and EW effects routinely operate in denied/degraded comms; if their tools require a persistent channel back to an analyst, they fail exactly where the mission is contested — same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: site markets capability breadth, not the connectivity model underneath it

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Low-friction Deployment' is asserted as a pillar but no ATO/RMF/CMMC/classification pathway is named for offensive cyber tools that would touch government networks
blind_spots.operator_reality: Exploit weaponization and CNO tooling require accreditation, classification handling, and often TS/SCI-level program access before a single tool reaches an operator — 'low-friction' is the opposite of the real timeline
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: marketing language optimizes for sounding fast, not for describing the accreditation gauntlet

blind_spots.blind_spot: No named program advocate or champion above the operator level — engagement is purely reactive ('Contact us about a mission need')
blind_spots.operator_reality: Operators liking a capability doesn't get it funded past a demo; without a program-office champion driving requirements and budget, an 8-person shop with 13 open reqs risks burning runway building tools nobody transitions
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: team is scaling engineering headcount, not acquisition/advocacy relationships, which don't show up on a careers page
